claims.text: The Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) is an open standard from OpenAI and Stripe for running checkout between an AI agent, a buyer and a business.
The ACP README labels the specification as beta.
The core ACP RFCs, including Agentic Checkout and Delegate Payment, carry the status Draft.
Newer ACP RFCs for capability negotiation, cart, discovery, product feeds, intent traces, affiliate attribution and marketing consent carry the status Proposal.
ACP is licensed under the Apache License 2.0, and the NOTICE file names OpenAI and Stripe as 2025 copyright holders.
The ACP GitHub repository agentic-commerce-protocol/agentic-commerce-protocol was created on 2025-09-29.
OpenAI announced Instant Checkout in ChatGPT and the open-sourced Agentic Commerce Protocol on 2025-09-29.
Stripe announced on 2025-09-29 that it co-developed ACP with OpenAI and introduced the Shared Payment Token.
MAINTAINERS.md lists OpenAI, Stripe and Meta as lead maintainers of ACP.
The ACP governance model was revised by PR 173 on 2026-03-10.
The ACP Technical Steering Committee has up to 7 seats, one per organization.
OpenAI and Stripe, as Founding Maintainers, appoint and remove ACP Technical Steering Committee members.
The ACP Technical Steering Committee had three members on 2026-10-11: OpenAI, Stripe and Meta.
Meta was added to the ACP Technical Steering Committee as seat 3 on 2026-04-24.
Significant ACP changes go through Specification Enhancement Proposals (SEPs) with a TSC sponsor, a 7-business-day public review and a simple majority TSC vote.
Standard ACP pull requests need two approvals from TSC members, and one may come from a recognized Domain Working Group member.
OpenAI and Stripe keep a reserve veto over ACP SEPs that can only block a change, never force one, and must come with a written explanation.
ACP has no foundation; its governance document states a long-term goal of moving to a neutral foundation once four conditions are met.
There is no fee to join the ACP Technical Steering Committee or a Domain Working Group.
The ACP TSC holds a weekly 30-minute meeting on Thursday and rotates a weekly triage lead with a 2-business-day initial response target.
ACP contributions require a Contributor License Agreement under a Collaboration and Governance Agreement dated 2025-11-21.
ACP corporate CLA signatories are Stripe, OpenAI, Adyen, Wix, commercetools, OpenCommerce Network, Affirm, Meta, Agentic Commerce Inc. (Catalog) and PayPal.
The ACP CLA list names OpenCommerce Network Inc., not nekuda, as a corporate signatory; a nekuda GitHub user appears among its authorized users.
PayPal signed the ACP corporate CLA on 2026-04-16 and Meta on 2026-03-19.
ACP versions are dates in YYYY-MM-DD format, and clients send the version in the required API-Version header.
The latest released ACP version is 2026-04-17, promoted by PR 227 on 2026-04-17.
The ACP repository has no GitHub releases and no Git tags; versions exist only as dated folders and changelog files.
Version 2025-12-12 renamed fulfillment_address to fulfillment_details and replaced fulfillment_option_id with selected_fulfillment_options.
The 2025-12-12 changelog says its breaking changes came from learnings from URBN and Etsy adapter implementations.
Version 2026-01-16 let merchants name their 3DS authentication provider and added adyen to the provider enums.
Version 2026-01-30 added capability negotiation, the payment handlers framework, the extensions framework and the discount extension.
The payment handlers framework in 2026-01-30 was a breaking change that replaced payment_provider.supported_payment_methods with capabilities.payment.handlers.
Version 2026-04-17 added Cart, the Feed API, Delegate Authentication, the /.well-known/acp.json discovery document and the MCP binding.
Version 2026-04-17 made the Idempotency-Key header mandatory on all POST requests.
Version 2026-04-17 added native orders with line items, fulfillments, adjustments and totals.
The last commit on the ACP main branch is 7fdd78d, SEP: Optional product URL on checkout Item (#281), committed 2026-07-18T04:51:51Z.
Eighteen commits landed on ACP main between 2026-04-24 and 2026-07-18, after the 2026-04-17 release.
No commit landed in the ACP repository between 2026-07-18 and 2026-10-11.
Unreleased ACP changes include suggested pricing on checkout create, fulfillment_details on complete, a feed_update_id on product upserts and an optional product url on checkout items.
Released ACP snapshot folders are edited after release: the 2026-01-30 checkout schema changed six times in February 2026 and the 2026-04-17 folder changed on 2026-05-01 and 2026-06-15.
The ACP repository package.json names the package @agentic-commerce-protocol/specification at version 0.1.0.
The package @agentic-commerce-protocol/specification is not published on npm; the registry returned 404 on 2026-10-11.
In ACP the merchant remains the system of record for orders, payments, taxes and compliance.
OpenAI is not the merchant of record in ACP; the merchant selling the goods is, and customers see the merchant's name on their card statement.
Under ACP the merchant handles refunds and chargebacks because it accepted the payment as merchant of record.
In ACP the agent calls the merchant's checkout endpoints and hosts the order webhook receiver at /agentic_checkout/webhooks/order_events.
Direct integration with OpenAI's Delegated Payment Spec is only for PSPs or PCI DSS Level 1 merchants using their own vaults.
OpenAI calls Stripe's Shared Payment Token the first Delegated Payment Spec-compatible implementation.
The Shared Payment Token is a Stripe product used with ACP, not part of the ACP specification.
The ACP discovery RFC allows a seller platform, for example acp.stripe.com, to host the discovery document on behalf of many sellers.
A 2026-04-17 checkout session requires id, capabilities, status, currency, line_items, fulfillment_options, totals, messages and links.
A 2026-04-17 create checkout request requires line_items, currency and capabilities.
From 2026-01-30 the ACP Item object has only id, name and unit_amount, with id required and no quantity field.
In ACP versions 2025-09-29 through 2026-01-16 the create request used items, and each Item required id and quantity.
The complete checkout request requires payment_data and may carry buyer, authentication_result, affiliate_attribution, risk_signals, marketing_consents and order_notes.
ACP payment_data carries handler_id, an instrument with a type and a credential holding a credential type and token, and an optional billing_address.
The ACP schema gives spt and wallet_token as example credential types; spt is not a fixed enum value.
ACP payment_data also has B2B fields: purchase_order_number, payment_terms (immediate, net_15, net_30, net_60, net_90), due_date and approval_required.
Every ACP PaymentHandler requires id, name, version, spec, requires_delegate_payment, requires_pci_compliance, psp, config_schema, instrument_schemas and config.
ACP payment handler names use reverse-DNS form, for example dev.acp.tokenized.card.
The seller-backed handler family is dev.acp.seller_backed.saved_card, dev.acp.seller_backed.gift_card, dev.acp.seller_backed.points and dev.acp.seller_backed.store_credit.
Seller-backed ACP handlers use requires_delegate_payment true and requires_pci_compliance false, so no card credential moves to the agent.
Version 2026-04-17 added optional display_order and display_name fields to payment handlers; display_order is only a suggestion.
ACP amounts are integers in minor currency units.
ACP Total types in 2026-04-17 are items_base_amount, items_discount, subtotal, discount, fulfillment, tax, fee, gift_wrap, tip, store_credit, total and amount_refunded.
ACP fulfillment option types are shipping, digital, pickup and local_delivery; pickup and local_delivery appear from 2026-01-30.

ACP MessageError codes in 2026-04-17 are missing, invalid, out_of_stock, payment_declined, requires_sign_in, requires_3ds, low_stock, quantity_exceeded, coupon_invalid, coupon_expired, minimum_not_met, maximum_exceeded, region_restricted, age_verification_required, approval_required, unsupported, not_found, conflict, rate_limited, expired and intervention_required.
ACP messages may carry a resolution value of recoverable, requires_buyer_input or requires_buyer_review, added in 2026-04-17.
ACP HTTP-level errors are flat objects with type, code, message and optional param, where type is invalid_request, processing_error or service_unavailable.
Since 2026-04-17 ACP servers SHOULD return a supported_versions array when they reject a missing or unsupported API-Version.
An ACP Order requires id, checkout_session_id and permalink_url.
ACP Order adjustments have defined types refund, credit, return, exchange, price_adjustment, cancellation and dispute, with dispute covering chargebacks.
ACP markdown content must follow CommonMark 0.31.2 and must not contain raw HTML, and agents must render it with raw HTML disabled or sanitized.
The Delegate Payment request requires payment_method, allowance, risk_signals and metadata, with an optional billing_address.
The ACP Allowance requires reason, max_amount, currency, checkout_session_id, merchant_id and expires_at.
The only Allowance reason defined by ACP is one_time.
Delegate Payment accepts only card credentials, with card_number_type set to fpan or network_token.
The Delegate Payment response returns a vault token id that starts with vt_, a created timestamp and metadata, with HTTP 201.
Delegate Payment risk signals have type card_testing, a score and an action of blocked, manual_review or authorized; since 2026-04-17 the array may be empty.
Version 2026-04-17 raised the maximum length of the card iin field from 6 to 8 characters.
The ACP discovery document requires protocol, api_base_url, transports and capabilities, and protocol.name is always acp.
Discovery capabilities.services can list checkout, orders, delegate_payment and carts, and transports can list rest and mcp.
An ACP Cart requires id, line_items, currency and totals, and its totals are estimates.
An ACP feed Product requires id and variants, and each Variant requires id and title.
The ACP IntentTrace reason codes are price_sensitivity, shipping_cost, shipping_speed, product_fit, trust_security, returns_policy, payment_options, comparison, timing_deferred and other.
ACP affiliate attribution requires a provider and supports first-touch at session creation and last-touch at completion.
ACP marketing consent uses marketing_consent_options on the session and marketing_consents with channel and opted_in on the complete request.
The only extension declared through the ACP extensions framework is discount, identified by name discount.
ACP discount responses can include applied discounts with allocations and rejected codes with reasons such as discount_code_expired.
ACP checkout requests require Authorization: Bearer, API-Version and, on POST, Idempotency-Key; Signature, Timestamp and Request-Id are recommended.
POST /checkout_sessions creates an ACP checkout session and returns 201 Created.
POST /checkout_sessions/{checkout_session_id} updates an ACP session and returns the full authoritative state with 200.
GET /checkout_sessions/{checkout_session_id} returns the session with 200 or 404 if it does not exist.
POST /checkout_sessions/{checkout_session_id}/complete must create an order and return status completed with an order id, checkout_session_id and permalink_url.
The ACP OpenAPI lists 200 as the success code for completing a checkout session.
POST /checkout_sessions/{checkout_session_id}/cancel returns 200 with status canceled, or 405 if the session is already completed or canceled.
A cancel request may carry an intent_trace with a required reason_code, and servers without intent trace support must still accept that body.
Delegate Payment is a single POST /agentic_commerce/delegate_payment endpoint that issues a token usable by the merchant's PSP only within the Allowance.
OpenAI prepares the delegated payment request with a maximum chargeable amount and an expiry based on what the user chose to buy.
When a seller requires 3DS it sets the session status to authentication_required and must include authentication_metadata.
If an agent completes a session in authentication_required without authentication_result, the server must return a 4XX error with code requires_3ds and param $.authentication_result.

ACP Delegate Authentication uses POST /delegate_authentication, POST /delegate_authentication/{authentication_session_id}/authenticate and GET /delegate_authentication/{authentication_session_id} for 3DS2.
In ACP Delegate Authentication the client reports fingerprint_completion as Y, N or U, using N after a 10-second timeout.
ACP sellers declare required interventions with capabilities.interventions.required and enforcement always, conditional or optional.
If an agent cannot handle a required intervention and enforcement is always, the seller should return a message with code intervention_required.
Capability negotiation in ACP uses intersection semantics: the agent declares what it supports and the seller returns the mutual set.
ACP idempotency errors are 400 idempotency_key_required, 422 idempotency_conflict and 409 idempotency_in_flight.
ACP servers must keep idempotency key mappings for at least 24 hours and must not cache 5xx responses against a key.
A replayed ACP response should carry the header Idempotent-Replayed: true.
The ACP cart endpoints are POST /carts, GET /carts/{id}, PUT /carts/{id} and POST /carts/{id}/cancel.
ACP carts are scoped to a single seller and have no status, no payment data and no capability negotiation.
The ACP Feed API is hosted by the agent and called by merchants, a push model with POST /feeds, GET /feeds/{id}, GET /feeds/{id}/products and PATCH /feeds/{id}/products.
ACP feed file ingestion uses metadata.json and products.jsonl and replaces the whole product set; promotions were deferred.
OpenAI's own feed API uses /product_feeds paths and adds a promotions API.
OpenAI recommends sending a full feed once a day by file upload and sending updates through the API during the day.
Onboarding product feeds into ChatGPT is limited to approved partners who apply through a form.
The ACP discovery document lives at /.well-known/acp.json, needs no authentication and should be cached with at least Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600.
Payment handlers are not in the ACP discovery document; they are returned per session on POST /checkout_sessions.
ACP 2025-09-29 defined five checkout statuses: not_ready_for_payment, ready_for_payment, completed, canceled and in_progress.
The checkout status authentication_required first appears in the ACP 2025-12-12 schema, not in 2026-01-30.
ACP 2026-01-30 added the checkout statuses incomplete, requires_escalation, pending_approval, complete_in_progress and expired, for 11 statuses in total.
None of the ACP RFCs define the meaning of the statuses added in 2026-01-30, and the checkout RFC still lists only the original five.
Stripe Shared Payment Tokens have the statuses active, requires_action and deactivated, and deactivated is terminal.
A Stripe SPT is deactivated when it is consumed, expires or is revoked.
ACP Delegate Authentication create returns action_required, pending or not_supported.
The 2026-04-17 ACP Order status values are created, confirmed, manual_review, processing, shipped, completed and canceled, after an edit on 2026-05-01.
ACP's MCP binding maps the five checkout operations to the tools create_checkout_session, get_checkout_session, update_checkout_session, complete_checkout_session and cancel_checkout_session.
The ACP MCP binding uses JSON-RPC 2.0 over MCP Streamable HTTP with arguments meta, id and payload.
In the ACP MCP binding, authorization moves to MCP server configuration and ACP errors use JSON-RPC code -32000.
The ACP MCP binding was added on 2026-02-19 by PR 139 and released in version 2026-04-17.
The ACP checkout RFC says TLS 1.3 must be used, while OpenAI's production guide asks for TLS 1.2 or later on port 443.
ACP request signatures are detached signatures over canonical JSON, base64url-encoded in the Signature header, with algorithms agreed out of band.
The Delegate Payment RFC gives Ed25519 and ES256 as example signature algorithms.
ACP order webhooks are signed with HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp, a dot and the raw body, sent as Merchant-Signature: t=<unix_seconds>,v1=<64_hex>.
The recommended timestamp tolerance for ACP webhook signatures is 300 seconds, and receivers reject failures with 401.
The ACP changelog says the Merchant-Signature format aligns with Stripe's webhook signature scheme.
ACP does not use verifiable credentials, user-signed mandates, RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures or on-chain components.
OpenAI says it intends to move entirely to network tokens as they become supported and that eligible cards are upgraded through network tokenization.
ACP agent and merchant pairs authenticate with bilateral bearer tokens; the spec has no agent registry or public key directory.
OpenAI asks merchants to allowlist its published egress IP ranges for ACP calls.
The Delegate Payment RFC says in one section that the client must sign requests, while its header list marks Signature as recommended and the OpenAPI marks it optional.
No GitHub security advisories or CVEs exist for the ACP repository as of 2026-10-11.
A 2026 Tamarin analysis models ACP together with x402, MPP and AP2 and reports 40 previously undocumented formal-consistency findings across the four protocols.
A 2026 paper says protocols such as AP2 and ACP lack interoperable, tamper-evident audit trails.
ACP has native spending caps through allowance.max_amount and currency.
ACP scopes a delegated token to one merchant and one checkout session through allowance.merchant_id and allowance.checkout_session_id.
ACP has no revocation endpoint; revocation exists in Stripe's SPT product.
ACP supports step-up authentication through the authentication_required status and 3DS2 Delegate Authentication.
ACP has no reputation mechanism.
OpenAI's docs say the Product Feed Spec and Agentic Checkout Spec carry no cardholder data, while direct Delegate Payment integration handles cardholder data and is likely in PCI scope.
OpenAI may require a PCI attestation of compliance before enabling production Delegate Payment access.
ACP implementations must not log full card numbers or CVC values.
OpenAI prohibits products such as adult content, alcohol, nicotine, gambling, weapons and prescription-only medications from ChatGPT shopping.
Stripe Shared Payment Tokens are available to agents, customers and sellers in the US, Canada and listed European countries.
ACP order webhooks use the event types order_create and order_update.
OpenAI's production checklist names the webhooks order_created and order_updated, which differs from the spec's order_create and order_update.
Version 2026-04-17 removed refunds[] from webhook order data in favor of adjustments[].
Stripe sends shared_payment.issued_token.requires_action, .active, .used and .deactivated events to agents, and shared_payment.granted_token.deactivated to sellers.
There is no public explorer, indexer or registry of ACP merchants; the ACP site says discovery mechanisms were still being developed.
Stripe SPTs carry usage_limits with currency, max_amount and expires_at, and the agent sets max_amount to the transaction total.
A seller uses an SPT by confirming a PaymentIntent with payment_method_data[shared_payment_granted_token], and Stripe clones the customer's original PaymentMethod.
Stripe lists cards, Link, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna and Affirm (limited) as SPT payment methods.
Stripe says it might use tokens from Mastercard Agent Pay and Visa Intelligent Commerce on a seller's behalf for SPT card payments.
Stripe's launch release says SPTs are scoped to a specific merchant and basket total.
Stripe's agent-side agentic commerce features are labeled private preview with a waitlist.
At launch, US ChatGPT Plus, Pro and Free users could buy from US Etsy sellers through Instant Checkout, with over a million Shopify merchants announced as coming soon.
Instant Checkout supported only single-item purchases at launch.
OpenAI said at launch that Instant Checkout items are not preferred in product results, though Instant Checkout availability is one ranking factor among several.
Walmart announced on 2025-10-14 that customers would soon be able to shop Walmart in ChatGPT using Instant Checkout.
PayPal announced on 2025-10-28 that it will adopt ACP, support Instant Checkout through the delegated payments API and run an ACP server for its merchants.
Stripe launched the Agentic Commerce Suite on 2025-12-11, naming platforms including Squarespace, Wix, Etsy, WooCommerce, commercetools and BigCommerce.
Microsoft launched Copilot Checkout on 2026-01-08 in the US with PayPal, Shopify and Stripe and said it is adopting open standards like ACP.
Microsoft's later agentic commerce page says Microsoft Merchant Center will support UCP and requires a UCP-compliant feed for Copilot Checkout.
Trade press reported in March 2026 an OpenAI spokesperson statement that Instant Checkout is moving to apps.
Shopify's president said on 2026-03-03 that only around a dozen merchants on the platform were selling through AI tools including ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot.
On 2026-03-24 OpenAI said the initial Instant Checkout lacked the flexibility it wanted and let merchants use their own checkout while it focused on product discovery.
On 2026-03-24 OpenAI expanded ACP to product discovery, with merchants sharing product feeds and promotions through ACP.
OpenAI named Target, Sephora, Nordstrom, Lowe's, Best Buy, The Home Depot and Wayfair as retailers integrated into ACP for discovery on 2026-03-24.
OpenAI said Shopify product data reaches ChatGPT through Shopify Catalog with no extra merchant work, and buyers complete purchases on the merchant's store.
OpenAI named Salesforce and Stripe as third-party providers that can deliver merchant feeds through ACP.
On 2026-03-24 OpenAI described a Walmart app in ChatGPT with account linking, loyalty and Walmart payments.
External checkout, where users finish on the merchant's own site, is the recommended and generally available checkout path for ChatGPT apps.
Checkout with the ChatGPT payment sheet is a private beta limited to select marketplace partners.
With the ChatGPT payment sheet, the widget calls requestCheckout and ChatGPT sends a payment-method token to the merchant's MCP server in a complete_checkout tool call.
OpenAI lists Adyen, Checkout.com, Fiserv, PayPal, Stripe and Worldpay as PSPs that support processing for the ChatGPT payment sheet.
Merchants with a PCI DSS Level 1 certificate can receive raw card data for the ChatGPT payment sheet by implementing the ACP Delegate Payment endpoint, including allowance constraints.
No source read says the general ChatGPT payment sheet token is an allowance-scoped delegated token.
Stripe's docs list UCP or ACP as the protocols used when sellers sell through agents with Stripe.
There is no official ACP SDK from OpenAI or Stripe; npm and PyPI packages named agentic-commerce-protocol are third-party type definitions published by Svix.
The ACP repository validates its JSON Schemas and examples in CI with scripts/validate-consistency.js and ajv.
OpenAI said on 2025-09-29 that merchants pay a small fee on completed Instant Checkout purchases and that the service is free for users.
OpenAI has not published a fee rate for ChatGPT checkout.
PYMNTS reported, citing The Information and a Shopify spokesperson, that Shopify merchants would pay OpenAI 4% on ChatGPT checkout sales on top of Shopify fees.
The same report said checkouts in Google's AI Mode and Gemini and in Microsoft Copilot carried no additional fee for now.
ACP itself charges no protocol fee; merchants pay their own PSP's processing fees because they charge the payment.
No SPT price appears on the Stripe agentic commerce and SPT pages read on 2026-10-11.
OpenAI said more than 700 million people use ChatGPT each week when it launched Instant Checkout.
No official ACP transaction volume, GMV or merchant count has been published by OpenAI, Stripe or the ACP project.
The ACP GitHub repository had 1,570 stars and 253 forks on 2026-10-11.
ACP has no documented relation to ERC-8004.
ERC-8183, a Draft created 2026-02-25, calls itself the Agentic Commerce Protocol but is an on-chain job escrow standard unrelated to OpenAI and Stripe's ACP.
ACP has no documented relation to x402; Stripe lists x402 with MPP for machine payments and ACP with UCP for selling through agents.
ACP has no documented relation to Visa TAP; ACP agents authenticate with bearer tokens and optional detached signatures.
ACP and UCP have no bridge or mapping specification.
ACP and UCP share five checkout status names: incomplete, requires_escalation, complete_in_progress, completed and canceled.
UCP uses ready_for_complete where ACP uses ready_for_payment.
ACP publishes discovery at /.well-known/acp.json and UCP at /.well-known/ucp.
Stripe says it is a member of the UCP Tech Council while also co-maintaining ACP.
Stripe's MPP integration accepts cards through Shared Payment Tokens, the same token family used as the first ACP Delegated Payment implementation.
Stripe's docs show SPTs used to pay MCP tool and app payment links, alongside MPP.
ACP has no AP2-style mandates, so it carries no signed proof of user intent beyond scoped tokens and the agent's own confirmation UI.
The Verifiable Intent project proposes carrying its credentials in ACP's extension mechanism; this is a proposal, not an adopted ACP extension.
ACP has no documented relation to Mastercard Agent Pay in the spec, but Agent Pay tokens can sit under Stripe SPT card payments.
The ChatGPT payment sheet uses an Apps SDK MCP tool named complete_checkout, which is not the ACP MCP binding's complete_checkout_session.
ACP RFC and OpenAPI request examples still send items with id and quantity, which do not validate against the 2026-04-17 schema that requires line_items without quantity.
The ACP checkout RFC still carries the header Version: 2026-01-16 after the 2026-04-17 release.
The ACP MCP binding keeps the idempotency key optional and lists request_not_idempotent, although REST 2026-04-17 made the header required and removed that error type.
OpenAI's docs say idempotency_conflict returns HTTP 409, while the ACP spec uses 422 for that code.
OpenAI's production checklist expects 201 Created on order completion, while the ACP OpenAPI lists 200.
The 2026-04-17 changelog lists the order status delivered, but the edited 2026-04-17 schema lists completed instead.
The 2026-01-30 ACP changelog deprecates a version 2026-01-22 that has no spec folder.
The ACP checkout OpenAPI describes the Signature header as an HMAC signature for webhook verification, which does not match the RFC's detached request signature.
The flagship ChatGPT Instant Checkout in its 2025 form was scaled back in March 2026.
OpenAI's developer docs still describe supporting Instant Checkout in ChatGPT as requiring three flows: product feed, checkout and payments.
ACP is not IBM's Agent Communication Protocol, which merged into A2A under the Linux Foundation in an announcement dated 2025-08-29.
The PyPI package acp-sdk is IBM's Agent Communication Protocol SDK, not an SDK for the Agentic Commerce Protocol.
ACP is not Virtuals' Agent Commerce Protocol, which Virtuals describes as the commerce layer of its on-chain agent economy.
ACP is not the Agent Client Protocol, a protocol for connecting editors to agents.
A 2025 survey of MCP, ACP, A2A and ANP uses ACP to mean IBM's Agent Communication Protocol.
The 2026 SoK on agentic commerce security lists an Agent Commerce Protocol next to ERC-8183, which likely refers to Virtuals' protocol rather than OpenAI and Stripe's ACP.
OpenAI's launch post says users confirm each step and that payment tokens are authorized only for specific amounts and merchants with the user's permission.
ACP lets agents embed commerce without becoming the merchant of record, according to its README.
The Stripe launch release says ChatGPT passes the SPT to the merchant, which can process through Stripe or another provider while using Stripe's risk scores.
